items.title: Amazon EKS announces end of support for Kubernetes version 1.28
items.summary: Standard support for Kubernetes version 1.28 on Amazon EKS ends on a published date. Clusters remaining on this version move to extended support and incur additional charges.
items.notes: Carries both risk types: the summary states end of support and names a Kubernetes version.

items.title: Amazon EKS supports Kubernetes version 1.32
items.summary: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service now supports a new Kubernetes version for cluster creation and upgrades.

items.title: AWS Lambda introduces a breaking change to response streaming defaults
items.summary: A default change affects how AWS Lambda handles streamed responses. Migration required for functions that depend on the previous buffering behavior.

items.title: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 13 reaches end of support
items.summary: Amazon RDS will end standard support for this major engine version. Instances not upgraded before the date are automatically upgraded during a maintenance window.
items.notes: Both risk types are correct: the summary states end of support and names an engine version.

items.title: Amazon Aurora publishes end-of-life dates for older engine versions
items.summary: The end-of-life schedule for several Amazon Aurora engine versions is now published.
items.notes: Hyphenated risk term and the Aurora alias, which maps to the rds service. The service-version-update expectation is a known recall gap: the configured term is 'engine version' and this text uses the plural 'engine versions', which phrase-boundary matching does not cover.

items.title: Amazon EKS announces end of support for an older Kubernetes version
items.summary: Non-breaking spaces and a typographic apostrophe in the cluster’s description must not defeat matching.
items.notes: Unicode normalization must fold NBSP to a space before phrase matching.

items.title: AWS Lambda announces a breaking change for the Node.js runtime
items.summary: Sanitized feed text can retain collapsed whitespace and stray punctuation: upgrade required for affected functions .
items.notes: Represents post-sanitization text, since raw HTML is not stored in the corpus.

items.title: Amazon EKS and Amazon RDS announce end of support for older versions
items.summary: Both Amazon EKS and Amazon RDS published end of support dates affecting existing clusters and database instances.
items.notes: Chapter 04 requires each service in one item to be evaluated independently.

items.title: AWS Lambda security bulletin describes a resolved vulnerability
items.summary: A security bulletin covering AWS Lambda describes a resolved issue and the CVE assigned to it.

items.title: Amazon RDS updates the end of support date for an older engine version
items.summary: This announcement was edited after publication to correct the end of support date. The corrected text still describes the same engine version.
items.notes: An edited item must still match; revision handling is announcement identity, not matching.

items.title: Amazon EKS reduces cluster creation time
items.summary: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service improves the time required to create a cluster. No action is needed.
items.notes: Service evidence with no risk evidence must not match.

items.title: Amazon Redshift announces end of support for an older cluster version
items.summary: This end of support notice covers a service that no declared profile contains.
items.notes: Risk evidence for an unconfigured service must not match a configured one.

items.title: Amazon RDS engine version now available in additional Regions
items.summary: A new engine version is now available in more AWS Regions. Existing instances are unaffected.
items.notes: The version rule excludes 'now available in', which is regional-availability news rather than a required action.

items.title: AWS publishes a customer story about platform modernization
items.summary: A customer describes migrating workloads to AWS and the operational practices adopted afterward.
items.notes: Generic AWS prose naming no configured service and no risk term.

items.title: Lambdas in functional programming: a breaking change in our tutorial series
items.summary: This article discusses lambdas as a language construct and includes a breaking change to the sample repository layout.
items.notes: 'Lambdas' must not satisfy the 'AWS Lambda' or 'Lambda function' aliases through a substring.
